name: What is the difference between pool remodeling and pool resurfacing?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between pool remodeling and pool resurfacing?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between pool remodeling and pool resurfacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool resurfacing is a finish replacement job. It focuses on the interior surface of the pool and usually involves draining, prep, and applying a new interior finish. Pool remodeling is a broader project that can include resurfacing plus tile replacement, coping replacement, equipment upgrades, plumbing changes, deck work, lighting, and design changes. That distinction matters because homeowners often compare prices without comparing scope. A resurfacing-only quote may look much cheaper than a full remodel, but it does not address failing tile lines, broken coping, outdated equipment, or cracked decking. If the goal is to modernize the entire pool, resurfacing alone may not solve the underlying problems. For older Los Angeles pools, remodeling is often the better choice when multiple components are reaching the end of their life at the same time. The best estimate should separate each line item so the homeowner can see what is cosmetic, what is functional, and what is optional.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool resurfacing replaces the pool’s interior finish, such as plaster, pebble, or quartz. Pool remodeling is broader and may include tile, coping, deck repairs, lighting, equipment upgrades, plumbing changes, or even reshaping parts of the pool. Resurfacing is one part of remodeling, not a full remodel by itself.
